title: Ordinary reduction and geometric inverse image preserve signed total tensor
statement: Fix l,E and the ordinary section-normalized limit comparison a of [def-sf-integral-system-canonical-bridge]. For every scheme morphism f:U→V and arbitrary completed-coefficient cochain complexes P,Q on V, let F be ordinary geometric inverse image on complexes, R_W ordinary whole-system quotient reduction, S the ordinary sequence inverse image, T_W integral total tensor, and B_W system total tensor. Let delta be the ordinary left-adjoint mate a.reductionPullComplex, psi_W the fixed strict reduction tensor map [lem-coef-tensor-reduction-strict-assembly], beta the inverse ordinary ringed total-tensor comparison and tau the ordinary sequence tensor comparison [lem-pur-sequence-pullback-tensor-cochain]. Then delta(T_V(P,Q)); S(psi_V(P,Q)); tau(R_V P,R_V Q) equals R_U(beta(P,Q)); psi_U(FP,FQ); B_U(delta(P),delta(Q)). Equality is in cochain complexes of strict coefficient systems, with all quotient transitions. No derived category, derived tensor model, K-flatness, flatness, completion or constructibility hypothesis is involved.

proof.text: Transpose the ordinary limit-comparison projection equations through the ordinary geometric and coefficient adjunctions. Joint monicity of the actual ordinary limit projections identifies the mate on iterated quotient and inverse-image units. This uses ordinary sections only, never faithfulness of derived finite evaluation.

Precompose in total degree k with each (p,q) tensor summand. Use the strict reduction map finite-component characterization and the sequence pullback tensor unit formula. The coefficient and inverse-image paths send every pure tensor to (b tensor x) tensor (1 tensor y). The ordinary scalar/geometric tensor calculation supplies the finite coefficient identity; linearity, balancing and sheafification extend it to each module summand.

Inverse image and scalar extension preserve the direct sums defining the total complexes. Their summand injections determine the degree maps. Both paths preserve input degrees, hence the signed differential, and their finite-component formulas preserve every quotient transition. This yields equality in the category of whole strict system complexes. Identity morphisms and zero complexes satisfy the same calculation.

theorem canonicalReductionTensorPullComplex
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (a : OrdinaryLimitModel l E) {U V : Scheme.{u}} (f : U ⟶ V)
    (P Q : CochainComplex (integralTowerModules l E V) ℤ) :
    let F := (integralOrdinaryPull l E f).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
    let R (W : Scheme.{u}) :=
      (pullbackTensorOrdinaryReduction l E W).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
    let S := (pullbackTensorSequenceInverse l E f).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
    let T := (coefficientTotalTensor.{u, u + 1, u} (ProEt.topology V)
      (completedIntegralCommRingSheafUnrestricted l E V)).obj (P, Q)
    a.reductionPullComplex l E f T ≫
        S.map (tensorReductionStrictMap l E V P Q) ≫
        (pullbackTensorSequenceCochain l E f).hom.app ((R V).obj P, (R V).obj Q) =
      (R U).map
          (proEtaleTensorPullbackTotalIso f ((PurCompactSupport.completed l E).ring V)
            ((PurCompactSupport.completed l E).ring U)
            ((PurCompactSupport.completed l E).pull f) P Q).inv ≫
        tensorReductionStrictMap l E U (F.obj P) (F.obj Q) ≫
        (coefficientTotalTensor.{u, u + 1, u}
          (coefficientSequenceTopology (ProEt.topology U))
          (coefficientSequenceCommRingSheaf l E U)).map
          (Prod.mkHom (a.reductionPullComplex l E f P) (a.reductionPullComplex l E f Q))
